correctness.rationale: For every integer d and N>=0 the exact 2026 kernel is the Fourier integral (1/2π)∫exp(idt)ρ(t)^N dt; N=n+v. Reflection yields real or imaginary branches by parity. Nonnegative discrete Poisson values, diagonal harmonicity and boundary P0=δ0 imply strict positivity at every interior even checkerboard site via propagation from a hypothetical zero along a connected path to the positive origin. On the opposite parity, the sine integral has strict sign of d because g=ρ^N decreases strictly and ∫g sin(dt)=(1/d)∫(-g′)(1−cos(dt))>0 when d>0; the d=0 case vanishes. The N=0 kernel is computed exactly. The zero graph forces any orthogonal family meeting interior to have at most two members. value.rationale: The exact zero locus of a canonical reproducing kernel is a natural function-space invariant and controls which interpolation evaluation functionals are orthogonal. Proving no additional zeros exist establishes a sharp qualitative boundary/interior dichotomy: unlimited orthogonal evaluation families on one boundary parity class, but at most two in any such family meeting the interior. This is a complete classification, not an arbitrary finite computation or a renaming of the partial zero list.
